I would keep my plan simple and steady. I have 14 mu, cotton is my main crop, and I also grow wheat and maize, so I would split the land in a way I can manage with my family and well water without taking too much risk. I would put 8 mu into cotton because that is my main cash crop, and I would keep 6 mu in the wheat-maize rotation so I still have grain and spread my risk. Since it is the start of the growing season, the wheat is already on the land from last autumn, and after wheat harvest I would plant summer maize on that same 6 mu. I would use better seed where it helps yield and stability, but I would not make the plan too costly. With irrigation from wells, I would irrigate wheat more, maize a moderate amount, and cotton based on key growth stages. I would use moderate fertilizer, not too light and not too heavy, because I want stable output and manageable cost. I would use rotary tillage for wheat and maize because it saves labor, and plough for cotton because I want a cleaner, deeper seedbed.
